breath.text: Welcome. Find a comfortable seat. Feet on the floor, hands resting. Let the eyes close, or soften your gaze.
Nothing to change yet. Just notice that you're breathing.
Now follow the rings. Breathe in through the nose as they grow. Breathe out slowly as they fall.
In for four. Out for six. Let the out-breath be the longer one.
Let the shoulders drop. Let the jaw soften. Let the tongue rest.
Feel your weight in the chair, and the floor beneath your feet.
When the mind wanders, that's fine. Come back to the next breath.
Now stop guiding the breath. Let it find its own rhythm.
Open your hearing. The sounds in the room. The sounds beyond it. Let them come to you.
You're here. Nothing to achieve. Nothing to prove.

intro: We begin the scales. Sit easily. Each perception is given to you once. Something will be there straight away, however small. Surrender to it.
release: Whatever came, you don't need to keep it. Release the body. Let the face soften. Let the breath drop.
Clear the mind. Nothing carries forward.
Now just hang out in your space. Nothing to anticipate. Nothing to prepare for. Simply here.
timed_release_lead: And when it's over, it's over. Let it go.
end_breath: You're centred. Carry this into the scales when you're ready.
end_scales: That's your practice for today. Nothing was forced. Carry that freedom with you.

lump.title: Lump of Faith
lines: Lump of faith. Sit calmly, and make sure you're in a calm place.
Now think of something.
Ask yourself: can I do that?
Now follow through, and do it. Tap when you've done it.
Return to your original place. Sense the glow of having succeeded.
Rest for a moment.
That's enough. Don't do too many of these.

freedom.title: Three Minutes of Freedom
lines: Three minutes of freedom. For the next three minutes, give yourself complete freedom. Think what you feel like thinking. Feel what you feel like feeling. Do what you feel like doing.
That's three minutes. Let it settle.

ana.title: ANA Breath Meditation
lines: Ana breath. Find a comfortable position, sitting or lying down. Sense the asana of your position. Let the body settle, and the breath soften.
Become aware of your natural breathing. No need to control it. Just notice.
On the inhale, say Ana, internally, or as a whisper. An-aa. Let it settle more and more in your centre.
On the exhale, repeat softly. Ana.
Continue this rhythm. Inhale, Ana. Exhale, Ana. Let the word gently mirror your existence. Not as a thought, but as a sensation. You're not affirming anything. You are simply being.
Now shift. Inhale, Ana. Exhale, Hu. The One. A living echo of: I am.
Now shift again. I, on the inhale. Am, on the exhale.
Let the words fade into nothingness. Just stay with observing the breath.
When you feel a sense of stillness, allow the eyes to gently open. Let the space arrive to you, without seeking. Let it become part of your sense of being completely singular in the here and now.

Allow the eye to land on a specific point in space. Let that point be admitted through the breath. Not stared at, but received. Follow the body's natural urge to move toward that point, slowly, intuitively. Don't decide in advance how the body will be when it arrives. Let the body decide. Let it settle. Tap when all of you is there.
All of me is sitting, standing, leaning, lying. When that sensation of unity is fully present, and only then, say out loud: I am. Notice what that feels like.
Now let the eye gently land on a new point, and repeat. Tap when all of you is there.
Not too many times. The point is not repetition, but to truly sense the asana of each shift. Let it go.
